builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Kai'Sa Void — the Nova runner-up
builds.summary: Second of 74 at NovaRiftbound #5. Every one of the 12 placed Kai'Sa lists is within 70% of the consensus: the most settled deck in the Radiance era so far.
builds.basis: YBE piorro - NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, #2 of 74, NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5. 95% consensus overlap.

changes.why: Kept as played; the placed lists barely differ from each other.

plan: Kai'Sa's legend exhausts to add one Power of any domain, for spells only — the deck is a spell deck with large units behind it.

The units are the payoff: Thousand-Tailed Watcher gives enemy units -3 Might this turn (to a minimum of 1); Brynhir Thundersong stops opponents playing cards the turn it lands; The Empyrean, new in Radiance, can Show Off a card to Predict and draw 2. Bilgewater Tracker, also new, deals 1 to each of up to 2 units on arrival.
Temporal Breach is Hidden: it banishes a unit and replays it at the same location, ignoring its cost — a reset for your own play effects as much as an answer.
builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: keep every opener; Energy spent turns 1–4 18.0 on the play / 20.3 on the draw; 3.0 units by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 0%; 7/5 runes fine.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Kennen Tempest — the Chaos majority build
builds.summary: The build most placed Kennen lists play (17 of 20 are within 70% of the consensus), from its best finish. The Haven winner is a different, Order-heavy deck — see its list below.
builds.basis: terrencem - Haven Online Challenger Series #5 - October 11th 2026 (Radiance Preview), #5 of 50, Haven Online Challenger Series #5 - October 11th 2026 (Radiance Preview). 90% of its main deck matches the consensus. Chosen over the #1 list because that one (35% overlap, Illaoi and Seal of Unity, 8 Order runes) is one player's build; this one is what the field converged on and still finished top 8.

changes.why: Kept as played. Copy the #1 list from the lists below if you want the Order build instead.

plan: Kennen's legend empowers whenever you play a card from anywhere other than your hand, then disempowers to give a unit Assault 2. The deck is built to do that every turn.

Lightning Rush looks at 3 and trashes the rest, and has Flow — playable again from the trash. Trifarian Captain looks at 4 and draws a cheap unit or gear. Nocturne, Horrifying can be played for one Power when you see it from the top of your deck. Each of those is a card played from somewhere other than your hand.
The trash filling up is the second engine: Rhasa the Sunderer costs 1 less for each card in it. Seal of Discord adds Chaos to get there.
9 Chaos / 3 Order. The simulator suggests bottoming 5+ cost cards in the opener.

matchups.note: No Radiance-era matchup records yet. The two events show Kennen beside Riven, Yasuo and Kai'Sa at the top; that is a field, not a matchup table.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: mulligan by bottoming 5+ cost cards; Energy spent turns 1–4 16.3 on the play / 17.4 on the draw; 3.4 units by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 1%; 9/3 runes fine.

builds.author: Claude
builds.title: Riven Exile — the Nova list
builds.summary: The list that won NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown #5 (74 players), kept as played. It is the closest thing to a proven Riven list that exists, and the other placed Riven lists mostly agree with it.
builds.basis: Sithis - NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, #1 of 74, NovaRiftbound's $2,000 Online Showdown 5, 2026-10-19. 83% of its main deck matches the consensus of the 9 placed Radiance-era Riven lists; 6 of those 9 are within 70% of the consensus, so this is one deck, not several.

changes.why: A winning list from a 74-player event beats a counted average. The options below are what the other placed lists do differently, for when you have a reason.
8 of 9 placed Riven lists play Ki Burst and most run 2; this list runs 1. Its additional cost is exhausting a friendly unit, which is the trigger Riven and Reckless Innovator want anyway.

5 of 9 placed lists run it (the #8 list runs 2); this list runs none. Reaction +2 Might, and if you Show Off a gear — this list has 7 (Blade of the Exile, Zhonya's Hourglass, The Good Stuff) — it readies up to 2 runes.

plan: The engine is exhausting your own units. The Exile makes units you play to battlefields you control enter ready, so they can act the turn they land. Riven, Broken Blade and Reckless Innovator both trigger 'when I become exhausted' — Riven buffs herself, then spends the buff to stun an enemy unit or ready again; Innovator makes a Gold gear token or lets you pay Chaos to draw 1 — and Stellacorn Herder draws whenever it moves.

So the turn the deck wants is: play to a battlefield you hold, move or attack with what just entered, and let the exhaust triggers pay you. Ki Burst's cost (exhaust a friendly unit) is another way to fire them on demand.

Interaction is held, not cast on curve: 3 Defy, 3 Discipline, 2 Rebuke, 2 Switcheroo, Gust, Star-Crossed, Ride the Wind, with 3 Zhonya's Hourglass protecting the unit that matters. Per strategy.md §0, scan for lethal both ways from 5 points before committing any of it.
Battlefields: Hunters' Circle, Emperor's Dais and Star Spring. Star Spring is in all 9 placed lists.

matchups.note: 12 placed lists, 3 top-8s across the two events: a 39-Spiderling deck that goes wide on one battlefield. Bedeviling Stranger returns an enemy unit when a battlefield has 4 or more units — a reading of the card text against their plan, not a tested result.
Won Haven and has the most placed Radiance lists (20). The Kennen box in guides/riven-exile-gauntlet.md was written before any Radiance results; treat it as a starting point.
No Radiance-era matchup records exist yet. Log your rounds in the journal and this gets rewritten from them.

builds.sim: Goldfish, 8,000 games: keep every opener; Energy spent turns 1–4 17.9 on the play / 19.9 on the draw; 2.8 units on board by turn 3; stuck on turn 3 1%; the 6/6 rune split is already the best. Consistency only — it plays no opponent.
